    #157885. Don’t Scan This Abroad: The QR Code Travel Scam Tourists Miss

    📅 01 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1584 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theplanetd ↗ Open Full Page

    Don’t Scan This Abroad: The QR Code Travel Scam Tourists Miss

    📅 01 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theplanetd

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • QR codes are everywhere when we travel now, on restaurant tables, parking meters, hotel signs, airports, train stations, and transit machines.
    • QR code travel scam happens when a fake QR code sends travellers to a fraudulent website.
    • Sources indicate that A scammer does not always need to hack a system or damage a payment machine.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    QR codes are everywhere when we travel now, on restaurant tables, parking meters, hotel signs, airports, train stations, and transit machines. This travel scam known as Quishing or QR code phishing is becoming the fastest growing travel scam warning out there. Most QR codes are legitimate, but scammers are using fake QR code stickers and fake payment pages to catch travellers when they are tired, rushed, or distracted.

    QR code travel scam happens when a fake QR code sends travellers to a fraudulent website. The code may be placed over a real QR code on a parking meter, restaurant table, hotel notice, airport sign, or transit machine, or it may arrive by text or email pretending to be a fine, toll, ticket, or check-in request. The safest rule is simple: Pause. Check. Then pay.Read out post: 20 Common Travel Scams and How to Avoid Them.

    Sources indicate that A scammer does not always need to hack a system or damage a payment machine. Sometimes they print a fake QR code sticker and place it directly over a legitimate code.

    From a quick glance, the sign still looks official. The logo may look familiar. The instructions may seem normal. The page that opens may copy the colours, layout, and branding of the real firm.

    Recent findings suggest that you think you are paying for parking, ordering food, checking into a hotel, or settling a toll. Instead, criminals may be collecting your credit card number, password, phone number, licence plate, email address, or other personal information.

    The FTC has also warned about fake traffic violation texts that begin with a QR code and try to scare people into paying a fake unpaid balance.

    The FTC has warned that scammers hide harmful links in QR codes to steal personal information, including by placing fake QR codes over real ones on parking meters.

    Many restaurants now use QR codes for menus, ordering, or payment. Most are legitimate, but travellers should still be cautious. This is the easiest travel scam for QR code phishing as everyone uses it.

    Recent findings suggest that A menu QR code should usually show a menu. Be careful if it asks for information it does not need, such as your passport number, banking details, hotel room number, or a password.

    Before scanning a QR code on a restaurant table, look at the surface. Does it look printed into the menu or table sign, or does it look like a sticker placed on top? If it looks raised, crooked, bubbled, or mismatched, ask staff for a printed menu or the restaurant’s official website.

    Parking is one of the easiest places for this scam to work because travellers are often rushed and confused.

    In a recent development, you may not know the local parking app. You may be dealing with another language. You may be worried about getting a ticket. That pressure makes a “scan to pay” sticker feel helpful.

    Before paying through a parking QR code, inspect the sticker, read the URL preview, and check whether the payment page matches the city, parking authority, or official app named on the machine.

    In a recent development, if anything feels off, do not use the QR code. Type the official website yourself, use the official parking app, pay at the machine, or ask local staff for help.

    Airports and transit stations are full of QR codes: Wi-Fi, directions, tickets, luggage storage, forms, lounge access, and service information. Travel scams often happen when travelers are in a hurry. If you need wifi, a taxi, some food, QR codes are often the easiest way to catch you off guard.

    Sources indicate that that does not mean every code is unsafe. It means you should slow down when a public QR code asks for payment, passwords, ID documents, or personal information.

    The FBI warns that malicious QR codes can send people to fake sites, steal victim data, embed malware, or redirect payments. The FBI warns that criminals can tamper with QR codes to redirect payments, steal login and financial information, or send people to malicious websites.

    The easiest way to avoid this scam is to build one habit before you scan a public QR code.

    Do not scan just because a sign looks official. Public signs, parking meters, table cards, and posters can be tampered with.

    If the message says you must pay immediately, avoid a fine, settle a toll, confirm a booking, or prevent a penalty, slow down. Urgency is one of the biggest warning signs.

    Before your phone opens anything, look at the QR code itself.

    Recent findings suggest that we call this the scratch test. You are not damaging the sign. You are simply checking whether the QR code feels or looks different from the rest of the surface.

    Canadian readers can also check the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security’s QR code safety guidance and report fraud through the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.

    Most phones show a preview of the website before opening the page. Read it.

    Look for misspellings, extra words, strange endings, random letters, shortened links, or a domain that does not match the manufacturer, hotel, restaurant, city, or attraction.

    Do not rely only on the padlock symbol. A secure connection does not automatically mean the site is legitimate. The real question is whether you are on the correct website.

    The FTC has also warned about fake traffic violation texts that include a QR code and pressure people to pay a fake unpaid balance.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

    I Am the Wildest Dream of Every Black and Brown Trans Woman Before Me

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that as an influencer, a lot of times I'm the only trans person—or the only trans person of color—in the room.
    • In a recent development, that’s especially true in this current political and cultural climate.
    • It’s been particularly challenging, too, as a trans person in the public eye; there's been many instances where my safety has been jeopardized.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that as an influencer, a lot of times I'm the only trans person—or the only trans person of color—in the room. It’s a lot of pressure, and there have been times where I have anxiety before going to certain spaces because I will question "Do I belong here?" But I’ve learned that that’s just the patriarchy and society trying to make us feel like we're not worthy.

    In a recent development, that’s especially true in this current political and cultural climate. The trans community, especially the Black and brown trans community, gets so much hate—that’s why I’m very offended when people say being trans “is a choice.” Like, living with and navigating these stigmas and mistreatments isn't something that someone would willing choose.

    It’s been particularly challenging, too, as a trans person in the public eye; there's been many instances where my safety has been jeopardized. When I get looked at, I'm thinking, They're looking at me either because I'm pretty or because I'm a viral trans person online. The differentiator is literally if I'm being chased home, which has happened multiple times. Since I speak out for trans women that can't speak for themselves, I'm also putting myself at risk. But at the same time, I think I can also make it safer for the next girl down the line.

    It's so rewarding being that person others can look up to. I love reassuring other trans women that they can do certain things or just live their lives authentically, loud, and open. But sometimes I'm like, Oh my god, how nice and easy would it be for me to just be silent and be in the background? But I don't think I was born to be a background girl. I'm front and center.

    And I think that the trans women before me would want me to be. The hard work that those women put for girls like me now, I have to show up for that. I think about trans women on the front lines of trans rights, like Marsha P. Johnson or Sylvia Rivera—they were front and center at Stonewall. They were the voices for many then, and there was so much more violence. The community was pretty much hidden at the time, too.

    It has been revealed that there's so much trans history lost, and Trans Day of Remembrance resurfaces those stories. A lot of times things get pushed under the rug because trans people are seen as not important to the media, or people in general, especially after all the propaganda that's been pushed out by certain administrations. But every year on this day, I learn about a different girl, especially outside of the U.S. I’ve learned so much about how some surgeries started because certain trans women needed gender-affirming care, and they paved the way for girls down the line.

    Industry observers note that education is the number one thing. I want people to know that your understanding of trans identities is not what you think and that there's a lot more to learn. There are times when I get frustrated because I see the stigmas and the rhetoric online that's really just misinformation, rumors, and lies that people make up about trans people. A lot of trans women have died because that ignorance can lead to trans violence. It's really sad to see. But we made it back then—and it was hard then—so we'll make it now. We're a strong community.

    The trans community, we show up for ours (for the most part). There's a couple spaces made for Black trans queer people, like the Black Trans Kitchen by Queen Jean—it’s really beautiful. And Gia Love created the annual Celebration of Black Trans Women Cookout. Trans women that make spaces like that really inspire me because they remind our community that we matter. And we as trans people need spaces where we can just be ourselves, and really show care to one another. Those spaces not only keep me humble, but also remind me of everything I've been through. It makes me feel so grateful and privileged to be alive today because a lot of girls don't make it.

    In a recent development, with the work that I do and everything I create, I want other trans women to see me and know that they belong and that they can be in those spaces too. I want to see more, especially more trans women of color, in positions of power and in rooms where you rarely ever see them.

    According to recent reports, I hope other trans women see that they can be their most authentic self, and that they can feel confident regardless of what anybody says. If you believe you're an amazing, beautiful person, it will reflect on the outside. I want people to feel that way and do that inner work because it's vital, especially for our survival as trans people.

    In a recent development, layering is the name of the game in fall and winter. For the next few months, you are not a person; you’re a living, breathing Russian nesting doll. You are encased in strategic layers of t-shirts, sweaters, scarves, light jackets, and significant jackets that you divest yourself of over the course of a day (or night). Like a knight donning his armor, you will spend this season dutifully putting on and taking off each of these individual pieces as you fight the seemingly endless battle against winter.

    According to recent reports, A few pieces are a given. A good tee certainly isn’t going anywhere, nor is a sweater. The specific kind of Big Coat you use varies depending on the guy and his style, but it’s nevertheless a guaranteed winter staple. Those middle layers can be a bit of a toss up, though, which is how you might encounter something like a quilted liner jacket.

    Industry observers note that once upon a time, these padded jackets served as the interior protective shell worn under World War II era flight jackets before they expanded into more mainstream outerwear. The quilted padding traps body heat, but doesn’t make the jacket so heavy that it just feels like another cumbersome layer. You can still wear it as a liner jacket—but lowkey, if it’s the right temperature, they also work pretty well on their own. So if you’re in the market for a new versatile transitional weather jacket, you’ve come to the right place.

    It has been revealed that if we had to pick one from this entire group, it would be this jacket from Buck Mason ... And it’s really not that close. Inspired by old-school mountaineering outfits, the nylon is woven in Japan, and the down fill has an exceptional warmth rating. Add a elastic cuffs and a fit that works layered underneath or overtop, it’s perfect.

    Look, layering’s great and all—but no one talks about how annoying and awkward it is when you get hot enough to take off one layer, but then are stuck just kind of holding onto it until you get the chance to put it down or hang it up. That’s not a problem with this packable Paul Smith shirt jacket. Let it do its magic to keep you warm. When you’re ready to take it off, simply collapse it down, zip it up, and stuff it away into your pocket until you need it again.

    Sources indicate that rains has a well-established reputation of balancing fashion and function with their outerwear, whether it’s their Esquire-editor favorite Fishtail Parka or this bomber liner jacket. Nothing beats a classic leather bomber...except maybe the rain (leather + rain = no bueno). That’s not an problem with Rains’ Banja bomber liner. You get that same edgy look, but with a slightly more practical construction. Plus there’s something sleekly minimal about the channel quilting. Layer it beneath your actual bomber or heavy coat of choice for optimal warmth all season long.

    Sources indicate that look, we love a good Dickies moment. They make some of our favorite pants of all time, not least of which because they’re mad affordable—though that’s a pretty big element to it. So naturally, if someone comes up to us asking for a high-quality and stylish quilted liner jacket at well under $100, we’ve got one word for ya: Dickies.

    Barbour’s been making sturdy outerwear that can withstand the rainy U.K. weather since the 1800s. And while they don’t strictly make a liner jacket, this lightweight—or “Flyweight,” as Barbour calls it—quilted jacket gets pretty close.

    Sources indicate that with a sleek, collarless design, this Fieldworth jacket can easily slide under any heavy coat. It falls more into “middleweight jacket” territory, meaning it’ll probably keep you toastier than some of the other options on this list—both on its own and when layered up.

    Industry observers note that if you’re looking for more of a typical fall/spring jacket, J.Crew’s PrimaLoft® jacket is where it’s at. The quintessentially Americana brand uses the down alternative to create a well-insulated transitional weather jacket you can layer with, or wear on its own.

    It has been revealed that look, all these other brands and designers are great and all—but Alpha Industries is the real deal. No like seriously. When the company was first founded in Tennessee in the 1950s, it was as a clothing contractor for the United States Department of Defense. These were the guys making those sexy flight jackets long before Tom Cruise shrugged one on in Top Gun. Their Deco Liner nods to the OG liners of yore, featuring a slim, collarless design that will integrate with additional layers. Wear the jacket by itself when you start feeling warmer, and let the whole world see the Alpha embroidery on the back so everyone knows this is some top of line shit.

    If you’re in the market for something lighter and less padded, opt for this cotton hunting jacket. The silhouette takes inspiration from vintage Czech military liners and traditional hunting gear to create a layer of outerwear breezy but still warm.

    Sources indicate that get two jackets for the price of one with this reversible number from Cos. You get all the benefits of a quilted coat, with the versatile sleekness of a classic collarless jacket.

    On the Couch with Leslie Bibb

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (888 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that since appearing in season three of HBO’s The White Lotus in 2025, American actress Leslie Bibb has had no problem keeping busy.
    • In a recent development, outside her day job, Bibb also happens to be a design enthusiast—she’s currently renovating the upstate Latest York home that she shares with longtime partner, fellow actor Sam Rockwell.
    • In a recent development, next up for Bibb is a starring role alongside Brett Goldstein in Amazon Prime series Escorted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that since appearing in season three of HBO’s The White Lotus in 2025, American actress Leslie Bibb has had no problem keeping busy. The North Dakota-born, Virginia-raised actress already had screen credits spanning from the Iron Man films to Apple TV+’s Palm Royale, but Bibb’s performance on Mike White’s hit series as one-third of a slightly toxic friendship trio spotlighted the actress’s knack for blending comedy and drama. Not to mention, her blunt bob served as hair inspiration for the masses. After The White Lotus, Bibb went on to guest star on HBO’s Hacks, landing her an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Comedy.

    In a recent development, outside her day job, Bibb also happens to be a design enthusiast—she’s currently renovating the upstate Latest York home that she shares with longtime partner, fellow actor Sam Rockwell. For the interiors, Bibb has teamed up with ELLE Decor A-List designer Shawn Henderson, who often pops up on Bibb’s Instagram account, attending birthday parties and surveying the concrete shell that will one day be a pool. In the kitchen, Bibb is partnering with LG Signature on appliances that gel with the new renovation.

    In a recent development, next up for Bibb is a starring role alongside Brett Goldstein in Amazon Prime series Escorted. She is also executive producing a show with HBO called The Rush Whisperer, a dark comedy about sorority rush. Together with the home renovation, she has trouble choosing what to highlight. “I’m just grateful that I’m able to juggle work and life and my relationship with Sam,” says the actress. For our On the Couch survey, she shares her greatest design inspirations, entertaining tips, and the artists that have her heart.

    According to recent reports, favorite Eras of Design: All of them... well, most of them. I'm not into cold, modern pieces from the 1980s or that shabby chic stuff. But I do like a house that isn't just one thing, that is a mix of eras and has warmth—a house that is inviting and says, “Come in, kick off your shoes, grab a drink and let's hang out.” And I love color.

    Favorite Sofa: I don't have a favorite sofa, but I do love an L-shaped sofa for watching TV so Sammy and I can be together but also have our own spaces to sprawl out.

    It has been revealed that maverick design style trick: I feel incredibly lucky to have my friend and fabulous interior designer, Shawn Henderson, as my secret weapon. Home renovations can be a nightmare, but having Shawn as my partner in crime has really made the experience so much fun. And let's be honest, the kitchen is the heart of any home. When I think of LG Signature, I think about how they design to honor your lifestyle rather than compete with it.

    Sources indicate that most beloved buildings: I love the Chrysler Building. It always takes my breath away. Also, there is a church where my parents are buried in the country and I just love it. It is so small and quaint and the view from its windows and the grounds just make me smile.

    Recent findings suggest that destination Museum: Musée d'Orsay because I get to see my favorite painting by Gustave Caillebotte called The Floor Scrapers. Honestly, wandering through museums or art galleries is one of my happy places so in any city you will find me making a pit stop to get an art fix and steal some inspo. I just saw the Krasner and Pollock "Past Continuous" exhibit at the Met and it blew my socks off.

    Recent findings suggest that go-to gallery or galleries: Any gallery, anywhere. Just go in and see what people are making. It will always inspire you in some way.

    Favorite Artist/Artwork: I love art and wandering around a museum or gallery is one of my safe spaces. I am mesmerized by pieces from Noah Davis. I love Helen Frankenthaler and Hilma af Klint. Also, I love Nick Cave and Danny Fox and Ramon Enrich and Peter Doig. The photographs from Sally Mann I love, too. Honestly, there are so many. I am in awe.

    Favorite getaway: Staycation...and hopefully at our home upstate once we are done!

    Recent findings suggest that best Host/Hostess Gift: I love to wrap a bottle of olive oil in a great kitchen towel so it is two gifts in one. I like a gift that can be put to use.

    Entertaining Tips: Always have a well-stocked bar with loads of options and feed your guests. Also, make sure you have a killer dance mix going because it ain't a party unless people start dancing. And if you have more than 25 people, hire a bartender. Otherwise you won't get to socialize and you will be just hosting all night and you will be exhausted.

    Cocktail or Mocktail of Choice: I am obsessed with this nonalcoholic Kolsch beer by Best Day Brewing Company. And winter is upon us, so a great martini. I am in Italy right now and am besotted with Negronis.

    Watch to Wear: There are two I really love: one I own that Sam gave me so long ago, my Rolex, and the other is one I want to get, which is the Cartier Baignoire.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A lot of us commiserate about commuting into the office, but there are a few positives to seeing your coworkers regularly, like finding your fellow movie buffs to discuss the latest films with, or bonding with the colleagues you grab drinks with after work. Another upside? Your group may do white elephant gift exchanges, Secret Santa, or at the very least, have an office holiday party. If you are doing a present swap this season, finding creative, affordable gifts for your coworkers could be tricky.

    First, there’s determining the budget; then it’s figuring out whether to get them something practical, fun, edible, or just plain silly. Our thoughtful recommendation is to get a gift they can use immediately or leave at work, like a cute tissue box cover, hand warmers (because the office is always cold), or even a small diffuser that makes the air around them smell better. We found 35 such items they’ll love, and if they truly want to, they could bring and use them at home too.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropologie has the most adorable mouse pads for the coworker who loves color and whimsy. This one is perfect for book lovers, but we also love the olive and sardines mouse pads.

    The office’s coffee and tea options are typically average, so make their mornings feel more premium with these fancy tea bags. “I got these at work one year, and I ended up falling in love with the tea brand,” Senior Commerce Editor Marina Liao claims. “Not only are the tea bags so cute (I feel bad throwing them out when I’m done), but the steeped tea is also highly aromatic and has depth—much better than the standard bags in the office.”.

    According to recent reports, the best gifts for coworkers are the ones they didn’t know they needed until they actually have the item in their hands—and can’t ever part with it. “Rechargeable hand warmers are a sleeper hit when I give them as gifts around the holidays,” indicates Managing Editor Sarah Esgro. “People always come back and thank me again because they didn’t realize how much they needed them. They’re sleek, can be easily tucked into a pocket, and don’t burn your hands the way that the disposable ones can. I even gave them to a coworker whose hands were chronically cold in the office, and she used them all year long!”.

    Industry observers note that make your manager laugh with this cheeky glass cup, complete with a wooden lid and a reusable straw. It's perfect for iced coffees, matcha lattes, and more.

    According to recent reports, every group has a crafty team member, which makes this LEGO set a good gift to give. They can build it at work during their lunch break and display it on their desk. Best of all, they don’t have to worry about their florals or greenery dying when they come back from the holiday break.

    In a recent development, the portable lunch box options for adults aren’t nearly as cute as the ones for kids, so we went on the hunt for a nice one and found this pick from Kate Spade New York. It packs just the right amount of style while still feeling functional, so if your coworker always brings their lunch from home, give them a lunch box they won’t cringe at.

    It has been revealed that professional chefs formulated this genius hand scrub. It neutralizes any lingering odors on your hands after a long day of cooking. “I snagged a bottle for a friend of mine who loves to cook, and kept a bottle for myself," Associate Shopping Editor Janae McKenzie states. "It’s basically replaced my typical hand soap; it feels so luxurious, and makes my hands smell and feel amazing, no matter how much garlic I chopped that day.”.

    Recent findings suggest that A blanket is a safe gift for anyone, and if your office tends to run super cold, like ours, a little fluffiness in their cubicle will be very welcome. This furry blanket from Madison Park adds some elegance and softness, making them feel a bit more comfortable at their desk.

    Sources indicate that for the days when work gets stressful, this easy-to-use Buddha Board is the perfect at-desk escape. With a refillable water brush, they can paint any design they choose on a canvas that evaporates in minutes. No muss, no fuss, just endless creativity to reset their brain.

    Industry observers note that we can't get enough of these cheeky cocktail napkins with the ingredients for a perfect Caesar salad. The coworker who's always shaking up a salad bowl around lunchtime will get a kick out of this.

    The personality hire is a key role in any office dynamic. Say thank you to the person who keeps things fun with this chic game box, complete with playing cards, dice, and a classy velvet lining.

    Putting together the staff holiday party is no easy task. Thank the coworker responsible for this finishing touch for the office Christmas tree: a set of scented tree stems. They complete the festive atmosphere by bringing the scent of fir and spruce to the office.

    This calming bonsai plant does well in low-light, so it's great for office environments. Brighten up their desk and give them something to look forward to when they come in each morning. You can even name it for an extra personal touch.

    Recent findings suggest that we all have one coworker who can't go a day without a Diet Coke. Help them bring that energy home with this cute candle that smells just like their favorite drink. It has a cola scent they'll love when they reach for their fizzy pick-me-up.

    Industry observers note that if your coworker travels for work a lot, gift them this flight essential that McKenzie swears by. “I never go to bed or travel without this thing anymore," McKenzie says. "I struggle with insomnia, and it gets worse when I’m not in my own bed. This is what gets me to fall asleep ASAP. The gentle weight on my eyes lulls me to sleep, and it’s a godsend on planes when I need to block out any stimuli.”.

    In a recent development, okay, how cute is this suitcase-shaped AirPods case cover? It's designed to look like an old-school metal carry-on complete with luggage labels from London and other stylish countries. It's definitely more economical than buying them an actual suitcase.

    Though there's no harm in buying pre-ground beans, any coffee-based drink will taste much more flavorful with freshly ground beans. So, if you sit near an admitted coffee snob, feel free to gift them this, which is small enough to grind one cup's worth of beans at a time.

    According to recent reports, it's hard to forget the day's tasks when they're jotted down on brightly colored notecards with funny headlines. This comes in a set of 12, so it's bound to last through the year.

    During the busy workday, it can be tough to remember to hydrate, which, of course, can lead to headaches, lack of energy, and a whole slew of annoying problems that only slow you down. So, if you want to help your coworkers (and perhaps yourself as well) to keep drinking, get them this water bottle, which is conveniently marked with hourly reminders.

    In a recent development, if there's a home chef in the office, they need this portable Crock-Pot. Now, they can bring their homemade soups, chili, or even queso nice and hot until they're ready for lunchtime.

    #157864. James Bond’s Favorite Luggage Brand Has Broken Its Own Rules

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (221 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    James Bond’s Favorite Luggage Brand Has Broken Its Own Rules

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (221 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, james Bond has always travelled in style.
    • In a recent development, now the company has done something completely left-field.
    • The fresh GT897 is Globe-Trotter's lightest case yet, and a significant departure from the design that made the brand famous.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, james Bond has always travelled in style. And while Daniel Craig's 007 was most immediately associated with his Aston Martins, Omega watches, and Tom Ford suits, his luggage of choice was Globe-Trotter, the Hertfordshire-based manufacturer whose cases have also found favor with everyone from Queen Elizabeth II to Kate Moss.

    In a recent development, now the company has done something completely left-field. After 129 years of making essentially the same kind of suitcase, it has changed the formula.

    The fresh GT897 is Globe-Trotter's lightest case yet, and a significant departure from the design that made the brand famous. Out go the traditional rigid frame and locks, replaced by a zip-around opening and softer, more streamlined silhouette.

    That noted, some familiar details keep it firmly on-brand: the vulcanized fiberboard, leather trim, nickel hardware, and those trademark exposed rivets. And the cases are still handcrafted in Hertfordshire.

    According to recent reports, at the moment available in two color combinations—bland-and-black and green-and-brown—the GT897 is priced at $1,395. A black-and-oxblood version follows in February.

    It's an interesting move for a organization whose USP has always rested somewhat on its refusal to change. Whether the upcoming James Bond will follow Craig's lead remains to be seen. But at least there's now a new option for packing his tuxedo.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Elledecor ↗ Open Full Page

    What Is a Thanksgiving Cactus? Your Guide to the Other Holiday Cactus

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (436 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elledecor

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By the time the garden has mostly called it a year, the Thanksgiving cactus is just getting started.
    • Recent findings suggest that you’ve probably seen one without knowing exactly what it was.
    • Sources indicate that the Thanksgiving cactus (Schlumbergera truncata) is a flowering cactus native to the forests of Brazil, where it grows on trees instead of in soil.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By the time the garden has mostly called it a year, the Thanksgiving cactus is just getting started. Its red, lavender, or soft salmon flowers appear at the tips of flat green stems, often right around the holiday, and its stems arch over the rim of the pot.

    Recent findings suggest that you’ve probably seen one without knowing exactly what it was. Thanksgiving and Christmas cacti often share a shelf and a label (“holiday cactus”), and both can flower in December. The giveaway is in the stems: the Thanksgiving cactus has little pointed teeth along the edges. And it’s far from the kind of cactus you’d put on your sunniest windowsill. It comes from the forests of Brazil, where it grows on trees in filtered light. Here’s what to know about the Thanksgiving cactus.

    Sources indicate that the Thanksgiving cactus (Schlumbergera truncata) is a flowering cactus native to the forests of Brazil, where it grows on trees instead of in soil. The flowers, which come in shades including white, red, lavender, and salmon-orange, typically open from mid-November through late December.

    Look at one of the flat stem segments. On a Thanksgiving cactus, the edges have pointed teeth; on a true Christmas cactus (Schlumbergera × buckleyi), they’re rounded, like the edge of a scalloped plate.

    Set it near an east-facing window or somewhere else with bright, indirect light. When the top inch of potting mix feels dry, water it thoroughly and let the excess drain. If you’ve tucked the nursery pot into a ceramic planter, lift it out to water so it doesn’t end up sitting in a puddle.

    While the plant is budding and flowering, keep the mix lightly moist. You can water less often once the flowers fade. There’s no need to repot it as soon as you bring it home; if it’s outgrown its container, wait until spring and go up one pot size.

    Recent findings suggest that in early fall, give the plant about 14 hours of uninterrupted darkness each night for roughly six weeks. A spare room that gets daylight but where nobody switches on a lamp at night works well. Cool nights—around 55 to 60 degrees Fahrenheit—also encourage buds to form. Once you see buds, keep the plant away from drafts and don’t let the potting mix dry out completely.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Above: Inside Carolina Herrera’s Miami flagship, a sculptural chandelier by artist Liz Oliver hangs suspended above a soft pink couch.
    • Industry observers note that in September, Carolina Herrera held an extravaganza of a runway show during New York Fashion Week, celebrating the brand’s 45th anniversary.
    • Opened on August 15, the 3,000-square-foot shop sits in the middle of the Miami Design District, with a dramatic arched entrance welcoming guests into the limestone-finished structure.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Above: Inside Carolina Herrera’s Miami flagship, a sculptural chandelier by artist Liz Oliver hangs suspended above a soft pink couch.

    Industry observers note that in September, Carolina Herrera held an extravaganza of a runway show during New York Fashion Week, celebrating the brand’s 45th anniversary. This past week, the festivities went further south, to Miami. Last Thursday night, creative director Wes Gordon and members of the city’s fashion and arts community gathered beneath a cherry-red awning to toast the brand’s newest boutique—and sixth official location in the U.S.

    Opened on August 15, the 3,000-square-foot shop sits in the middle of the Miami Design District, with a dramatic arched entrance welcoming guests into the limestone-finished structure. Designed in collaboration with interior designers Brandi Howe and Jessica Hyland of Hyland Studio, the store is bursting with color and feminine details—soft pink travertine covers the floor while furnishings feature red and pink accents. In the center of the main salon, a custom pink sofa with graceful curvature offers an elegant seat; in another area, the same red awning from the boutique’s entrance reappears suspended over a pair of regal armchairs.

    “The Carolina Herrera woman is bold, elegant, and joyful. She embraces color, expresses herself with confidence, and never shies away from making an entrance,” says Gordon.

    It has been revealed that but the new store is not only an ode to the Carolina Herrera brand but also to other female creatives. On view throughout the space are artworks commissioned specifically for the boutique as a part of the Carolina Herrera for Women in the Arts initiative. In the main salon, Los Angeles-based artist Liz Oliver designed a rose-colored textile installation that doubles as a sculptural chandelier. Elsewhere, ceramic planters made by the women-owned Choplet Ceramics are on display. Throughout the boutique, a recurring custom floral motif by Argentine artist Constanza Vallese appears on vases and tables.

    In a recent development, in raising a glass to the boutique, guests at last Thursday’s event honored both the Carolina Herrera woman and her new city. “Her energy is magnetic—much like the spirit of Miami,” claims Gordon. “It feels entirely natural that we should open our next home here.”.

    #157845. The Beyond Devastating ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ Ending, Explained

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (806 w)

    The Beyond Devastating ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ Ending, Explained

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (806 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that crying too hard at the end of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to fully grasp those final scenes?
    • It should come as no surprise that Haymitch wins the Hunger Games.
    • What we didn’t totally know before the release of this book, and subsequent film, was that Haymitch teamed up with other recent victors like Beetee, Mags, and Wiress (as well as future gamemaker Plutarch Heavensbee) to try and take down the games from within.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that crying too hard at the end of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to fully grasp those final scenes? It can happen to the best of us. Let’s break down the ending of Sunrise on the Reaping to make sure you didn’t miss anything, including some of the things that Suzanne Collins’ book explains in a tiiiiiny bit more detail.

    It should come as no surprise that Haymitch wins the Hunger Games. You should know that going in, even if you haven’t read Sunrise on the Reaping. When we first met the character in The Hunger Games, he was Katniss and Peeta’s mentor because he was District 12’s only living victor.

    What we didn’t totally know before the release of this book, and subsequent film, was that Haymitch teamed up with other recent victors like Beetee, Mags, and Wiress (as well as future gamemaker Plutarch Heavensbee) to try and take down the games from within. As we first learned that in Catching Fire, the flaws that Haymitch found in the arena contributed to his victory.

    President Snow does not like to be beaten and finds creative ways to get revenge against those who double-cross him. We see that early on with Beetee’s son Ampert, who gets reaped to punish Beetee for how he won his games. We see it later with Peeta and Katniss. And Haymitch is allowed to return home at the expense of his mother, brother, and girlfriend. All three die horrifically as soon as he gets back. As many have said: Haymitch didn’t drink enough.

    At the end of the film, we see how President Snow’s revenge against Haymitch’s community causes him to spiral fast. With his family and girlfriend dead, in addition to the PTSD from surviving the Hunger Games, he becomes inconsolable and addicted to sleeping syrup. It does not help that he is the only person living in Victor’s Village; because District 12’s only other victor, Lucy Gray Baird, went missing 40 years prior.

    One day, Plutarch comes to visit Haymitch ahead of his victory tour to film an upgrade for the Capitol News, and they have a chat. (In the book, this conversation happens during the tour.) He wants Haymitch to keep working with them to overthrow the Capitol. He refuses. “I am living proof the Capitol always wins,” Haymitch claims. “You need someone different from me.”.

    Plutarch insists that they need someone exactly like him, actually. Even if it takes generations and they don’t get to see the results, they have to keep imagining a different future so that one day it comes true. It doesn’t make them heroes. It doesn’t even make them good people. But they’re trying.

    In a recent development, haymitch drifts away from two of his only friends, Burdock Everdeen and Asterid March. If you couldn’t tell from their names, or didn’t hear what they call their infant daughter, yes! Those are Katniss’ parents. (Also, yes! Burdock Everdeen is a member of the Covey. That’s why he sings one of Lucy Gray’s songs, "The Old Therebefore," at the funeral for District 12’s tributes. One day, he’ll change the course of history by teaching her “The Hanging Tree.”.

    The main reason that Haymitch cuts himself off is grief and guilt. He wants to be alone with his pain. Losing the people he was closest too makes him feel like he doesn’t deserve to be close to anyone, and maybe shouldn’t for their own protection. Movie protagonists are always thinking that, aren’t they? Like, okay Spider-Man! Whatever you say!

    But the book reveals another, even more devastating reason: when baby Katniss grows up and starts wearing her hair in pigtail braids, she looks just like Haymitch’s “sweetheart” and first ally, Louella.

    As we know from reading and watching The Hunger Games, the rebellion in Panem did eventually find the right victors to raise an army and end the games for good in District 12’s own Peeta Mellark and Katniss Everdeen. They were able to finally implement the looks that Beetee, Wiress, and the other victors had been testing since the second Quarter Quell, if not before.

    Recent findings suggest that without even knowing it, Peeta and Katniss helped Haymitch keep his promise to Lenore Dove. So, of course, the story has to end with them. We see Haymitch, again played by Woody Harrelson, finally celebrating his birthday with no reapings. In Collin’s novel, Haymitch tells Katniss and Peeta about Lenore Dove in order to add her to a District 12 book of memories they’re putting together. Katniss gifts him goose eggs to hatch and raise. The film, however, takes a simpler approach, and just shows old man Haymitch greeting his former mentees before going to spend some alone time with the geese. He’s finally earned some peace.

    20 White Elephant Gifts Everyone Will Fight Over

    📖 0% read

    • In a recent development, luckily, that still leaves plenty of fun, affordable, crowd-pleasing gifts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that if you’re reading this, there’s probably a holiday gift exchange on your calendar coming up. Maybe your boss organized one for the office, or maybe it’s the doing of that one friend who loves hosting so much they’d throw a party for Arbor Day. Either way, you’re probably wondering: What the heck do I bring to this thing?

    There are a few rules to this game. First, there’s likely a price cap, so we’re keeping everything under $100. (If your white elephant involves luxury gifts, we’d love to be a fly on that very well-appointed wall.) Second, your gift should be something just about anyone would be excited to unwrap. That rules out clothes and shoes with specific sizes, phone cases for whatever iPhone model is presently in circulation, and franchise merch that assumes your giftee has seen every Marvel movie or follows football.

    In a recent development, luckily, that still leaves plenty of fun, affordable, crowd-pleasing gifts. We’ve rounded up our favorites below, so pick one, wrap it up, and take all the credit when everyone starts fighting over it.

    Who doesn’t like waffles? A waffle-maker that’s easy to use and easy to store is for sure going to be a slam dunk at the gift exchange.

    A cute felt ornament is a great gift that’s sort of holiday-themed, but also makes a fun gift for any occasion. It will take their Christmas tree to the next level—and even if they don’t celebrate Christmas, they can hang this little guy on a doorknob, at their desk, etc.

    In a recent development, jigsaw puzzles have always been a popular pastime, but people (ahem, my mom and sister) have especially taken up puzzling since the pandemic. Piecework makes some of my favorite puzzles, like this quirky peppermint-themed one.

    Whether they drink coffee or tea, this leakproof tumbler will no doubt become their go-to drink vessel. Coffee for the morning commute? Check. Hot tea for an afternoon pick-me-up? Check. A glass of wine with dinner? Sure, why not. The Strova has all that covered (literally).

    In these cold-weather months, hand cream is a must. This luxurious one from Homecourt smells like cedarwood smoke, sweet cardamom, cinnamon, and white leather.

    In a recent development, everyone wants a home that smells good. Aera’s aroma diffuser will make that happen. Yes, it’s at the upper limit price-wise, but it’s bound to be the gift everyone wants.

    In a recent development, just any old liquor won’t cut it, but Fords Sloe Gin is perfect for the holidays. Whoever gets this bottle will be making Sloe Gin Fizzes all winter long, and if you’re lucky, they’ll invite you over for one.

    This rechargeable candle lighter is both practical and artful—it eliminates the need for matches altogether, and it looks classy next to a candle.

    Yes, a candle is a classic gift exchange option, but don’t just go for your run-of-the-mill Yankee Candle; get one that will make their home smell like a winter wonderland.

    According to recent reports, who wouldn’t want a tiny printer that can instantly print photos from your phone? This one comes with a paper roll so your giftee can get started printing as soon as they open this awesome present.

    Everyone needs a hat in the winter, so why not make it a nice cashmere beanie from Quince? They won’t know you only spent $35 on it—that’s how luxurious it feels.

    In a recent development, this set of extra virgin olive oil and balsamic vinegar from Kosterina is a great gift for anyone who cooks, whether they’re a beginner or a professional chef. And the fun holiday packaging is a plus!

    Another thing everyone needs? A toiletry bag. No matter where they’re going this holiday season, they’ll need a place to pack their toothbrush, comb, razor, and whatever other bathroom essentials they use. Why not pack them in this cute pouch from Brooklinen?

    Everyone is getting into peptides now. Make it easy for whoever gets this gift to start their peptide journey with this duo from Naturium.

    Industry observers note that gloves don’t have to be boring. Verloop makes fun, colorful pairs that, yes, are touchscreen compatible. Everyone will want to get their hands on (and in) these.

    A tiny record player that can actually play (tiny) records? It’s the dream of any music lover who lives in a small apartment!

    Recent findings suggest that help someone get organized with a fun planner they’ll actually want to use. Burga has tons of cool patterns, so choose one you think will appeal to most people.

    Recent findings suggest that A tote bag is the versatile catch-all bag everyone should have at least one of. And these mini ones from Steele are so cute and will last forever.

    Recent findings suggest that if you’re going to go with a food gift, make it a Classic Panettone holiday cake from Eataly. Everyone will want a piece of this.

    According to recent reports, pretty much anything from the MoMA Design Store is guaranteed to be a hit, and it will probably be the most unique gift at the party. Take these colorful crystal glasses, for example. Who wouldn’t want these in their kitchen?
